applications.title: Applications
applications.description: Empowering researchers and laboratories with innovative biotechnology solutions that simplify workflows, enhance precision and support scientific discoveries.

categories.name: Molecular Biology
categories.description: Molecular biology opens a window into the tiny biological mechanisms that shape every living organism. It brings together scientific research and advanced laboratory methods to investigate how genetic material and cellular molecules interact, communicate, and influence biological functions.

subcategories.name: Nucleic Acid Purification
subcategories.description: Get pure, ready-to-use DNA and RNA with LightCells's isolation kits for plasmids, genomic DNA, RNA, and gel extraction. Designed to support accurate results in PCR, cloning, sequencing, and expression studies.

items.name: Plasmid Isolation Kit
items.description: Isolate pure plasmid DNA from bacterial cultures with this ready-to-use kit. It removes genomic DNA, proteins, and cell debris, giving you clean plasmids for cloning, sequencing, and other downstream applications.

subcategories.name: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis
subcategories.description: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis is a laboratory technique used to separate DNA fragments based on their size using an electric field. It is commonly used after PCR to visualize and verify amplified DNA products, making it essential for DNA analysis, cloning, and molecular biology research.

subcategories.name: Cloning
subcategories.description: Cloning is a molecular biology technique used to create identical copies of specific DNA fragments by inserting them into vectors such as plasmids. It enables gene replication and is widely used in genetic research, gene expression studies, and recombinant protein production.

subcategories.name: PCR
subcategories.description: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is a powerful technique used to amplify a specific segment of DNA, generating millions of copies from even a tiny initial sample. The process involves repeated cycles of denaturation, annealing, and extension carried out by a heat-stable DNA polymerase enzyme. PCR is essential in genetic research, medical diagnostics, forensics, and cloning, enabling accurate detection, analysis, and manipulation of DNA sequences.

subcategories.name: qPCR
subcategories.description: Quantitative PCR (qPCR), also known as real-time PCR, is a sensitive molecular technique that monitors DNA or RNA amplification using fluorescent signals. It enables accurate quantification of genetic material and is widely used in gene expression studies, pathogen detection, and molecular diagnostics.

categories.name: Protein Biology
categories.description: Proteins are essential components of living systems, contributing to the structure, activity, and regulation of cells. Protein biology investigates how these molecules are produced, acquire their functional shapes, and interact with other cellular components to support processes such as communication between cells, energy production, and immune defence.

subcategories.name: Extraction
subcategories.description: Extraction is a fundamental laboratory process used to isolate and purify specific compounds from biological or chemical samples. Common techniques include liquid–liquid extraction, solid-phase extraction, and nucleic acid extraction (DNA/RNA). These methods are widely used in molecular biology, diagnostics, pharmaceutical research, and analytical applications.

subcategories.name: Purification
subcategories.description: Protein purification is a laboratory process used to isolate specific proteins from complex biological samples. Techniques such as affinity, ion-exchange, and size-exclusion chromatography, along with precipitation and electrophoresis, help remove impurities and obtain purified proteins for research, analysis, and therapeutic applications.

subcategories.name: Quantification
subcategories.description: Quantification is the process of measuring the concentration or amount of biomolecules such as DNA, RNA, and proteins in a sample. Techniques including spectrophotometry, fluorometry, and colorimetric assays provide accurate measurements for molecular biology research, sample analysis, and quality control.

subcategories.name: Concentration
subcategories.description: Concentration is the measurement of the amount of a substance present in a given volume of solution. In molecular biology, it is commonly used to determine DNA, RNA, and protein levels, ensuring accurate sample preparation, experimental consistency, and reliable research results.

subcategories.name: SDS-PAGE
subcategories.description: SDS-PAGE is a protein analysis technique that separates proteins according to their molecular weight using a polyacrylamide gel. SDS gives proteins a uniform negative charge, allowing them to migrate through the gel under an electric field for protein profiling, purity assessment, and molecular weight analysis.

subcategories.name: Western Blotting
subcategories.description: Western blotting is a protein detection technique used to identify specific proteins following SDS-PAGE separation. Proteins are transferred onto a membrane and detected using target-specific antibodies through chemiluminescence or colorimetric methods, enabling protein expression analysis and validation.

subcategories.name: ELISA
subcategories.description: ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) is an immunological technique used to detect and quantify specific targets through antigen–antibody binding. The antigen acts as the target, while the antibody specifically recognizes and binds to it. An enzyme-linked detection system produces a measurable colorimetric signal for diagnostic and research applications.

subcategories.name: Antibodies
subcategories.description: Antibodies are specialized proteins that specifically recognize and bind to target molecules such as proteins, peptides, hormones, and pathogen antigens. They are widely used to detect and quantify specific targets in research and diagnostic techniques such as Western blotting, ELISA, and immunohistochemistry.

categories.name: Cell Culture
categories.description: Cell culture provides researchers with a way to maintain and investigate living cells in a carefully managed laboratory environment. By supplying suitable nutrients, growth media, and environmental conditions, scientists can support cell survival, development, and multiplication outside the organism from which the cells originate.

categories.name: Analytical Chemistry
categories.description: Analytical chemistry helps researchers discover what a material contains and determine the quantity of its individual chemical constituents. Through carefully designed laboratory investigations, scientists can examine the composition, purity, and characteristics of samples with accuracy and consistency.

categories.name: Organic Synthesis
categories.description: Organic synthesis enables scientists to create new carbon-based molecules by combining simpler chemical substances through carefully planned reactions. By selecting suitable starting materials, reaction conditions, and chemical pathways, researchers can develop compounds with specific structures and characteristics for further study and practical use.

subcategories.name: Amino Acids, Resins & Reagents for Peptide Synthesis

categories.name: Material Science
categories.description: Materials science explores how different materials are formed, how their internal structures influence their behaviour, and how they can be improved for specific applications. By examining materials at microscopic and atomic scales, researchers can better understand characteristics such as durability, thermal stability, electrical performance, strength, and resistance to environmental conditions.

subcategories.name: High Purity Metals Oxides and Salts

categories.name: Filtration
categories.description: Filtration is a separation technique used to remove unwanted particles from fluids by directing a mixture through a material designed to retain selected components. Depending on the application, filter media such as membranes, fibrous materials, and porous surfaces can be used to achieve the required level of separation.

Our range supports the preparation of purified and ultrapure water for laboratories involved in pharmaceutical development, clinical testing, academic studies, industrial processes, and scientific research.
